question: What did the medieval term "Raqs" mean?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dancing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The medieval term "**Raqs**" means **belly dancing**.
 
• It features movements of the hips and torso.
 
• With the migration of the **Gypsy tribes**, it began more than 5000 years ago in **Egypt **and spread throughout the Middle East.
 
• Eventually, they arrived in **Europe**, the birthplace of the well-known Gypsy dance, **Flamenco**.
 
• **Belly dancing** and modern **flamenco **share a lot of **similarities**.
 
• It originated from a religious dance performed as a **fertility ritual** by priestesses and is a dance that was **part of the birthing rite **and helped women get ready for labor.
 
• It was inspired by a social dance from ancient **Egypt**.
